NAME: Payment Method Mix per Merchant
DESC:
A payment service provider wants a wide report with one row per merchant and one amount column per payment method, to feed a dashboard.

Input

payments_df

column type description
payment_id string never null
merchant_id string never null
method string free text, e.g. "card", " Card ", "WALLET", "bank_transfer", "crypto"; may be null
amount double strictly positive, never null
status string succeeded, failed or refunded (always lowercase)

Rows that share a payment_id are exact duplicates.

Rules

  1. Only succeeded payments count. Each payment_id counts once.
  2. The method is trimmed and lowercased. card, wallet and bank_transfer are kept as they are; any other value, including null, becomes other.
  3. One output row per merchant with at least one counted payment. A merchant without any counted payment does not appear.
  4. The four amount columns always exist, even if no payment in the input uses that method; a method that a merchant did not use has an amount of 0.0, not null.
  5. All amounts are rounded to 2 decimals. card_share_pct is 100 * card amount / total amount, rounded to 1 decimal.

Output

Exactly these columns, in this order:

column type description
merchant_id string
n_payments long number of counted payments
card_amount double
wallet_amount double
bank_transfer_amount double
other_amount double
total_amount double sum of the four amounts
card_share_pct double

Rows are sorted by total_amount descending, then merchant_id ascending.

Example

payments_df

payment_id merchant_id method amount status
P1 M1 "card" 100.0 succeeded
P2 M1 " Card " 50.0 succeeded
P3 M1 "wallet" 25.5 succeeded
P4 M1 "card" 70.0 failed
P5 M2 "bank_transfer" 300.0 succeeded
P6 M2 "crypto" 20.0 succeeded
P7 M2 null 10.0 succeeded
P8 M3 "card" 40.0 refunded
P2 M1 " Card " 50.0 succeeded

Expected output

merchant_id n_payments card_amount wallet_amount bank_transfer_amount other_amount total_amount card_share_pct
M2 3 0.0 0.0 300.0 30.0 330.0 0.0
M1 3 150.0 25.5 0.0 0.0 175.5 85.5

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(payments_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. No pandas, no collect(), no Python UDFs.
  • payments_df has up to 10^7 rows.
  • The returned DataFrame may be empty; its 8 columns and their types must still match the specification.
STARTER:

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

METHODS = ["card", "wallet", "bank_transfer", "other"]


def solve(payments_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Paiements réussis, doublons exacts supprimés, méthode normalisée.
    m = F.lower(F.trim(F.col("method")))
    ok = (
        payments_df
        .filter(F.col("status") == "succeeded")
        .dropDuplicates(["payment_id"])
        .withColumn("method_norm",
                    # isin(null) est null => otherwise : une méthode null tombe bien dans 'other'
                    F.when(m.isin("card", "wallet", "bank_transfer"), m).otherwise(F.lit("other")))
    )

    # 2. Pivot avec la liste EXPLICITE des valeurs : les 4 colonnes existent toujours.
    pivoted = (
        ok.groupBy("merchant_id")
        .pivot("method_norm", METHODS)
        .agg(F.sum("amount"))
        .fillna(0.0, subset=METHODS)                     # combinaison absente => null => 0.0
    )
    counts = ok.groupBy("merchant_id").agg(F.count(F.lit(1)).alias("n_payments"))

    total = F.col("card") + F.col("wallet") + F.col("bank_transfer") + F.col("other")
    result = (
        pivoted.join(counts, "merchant_id")
        .withColumn("total", total)
        .select(
            "merchant_id",
            "n_payments",
            F.round("card", 2).alias("card_amount"),
            F.round("wallet", 2).alias("wallet_amount"),
            F.round("bank_transfer", 2).alias("bank_transfer_amount"),
            F.round("other", 2).alias("other_amount"),
            F.round("total", 2).alias("total_amount"),
            F.round(F.col("card") * 100 / F.col("total"), 1).alias("card_share_pct"),
        )
    )
    return result.orderBy(F.col("total_amount").desc(), F.col("merchant_id").asc())
